title: Sunshine: canonical unit enable and security-floor bump
head: d1edce37e4ed
workflow: Opus full review, Sol boundary hunter, Opus self-check of the draft, editorial check, batch gates

leads.summary: Existing Sunshine installs keep the old Hyprland autostart process after switching to systemd-only installs
leads.consequence: The previous installer appended o.launch_on_start("sunshine") to ~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua. The new installer stops adding it, but neither it nor the only new migration removes it. On a previously successful install, Hyprland still runs that command on each session start alongside the enabled user service; reinstall also leaves it. Only a separate uninstall strips it. The user still sees the competing-start failure until they remove the old line, uninstall, explicitly refresh all Hyprland config, or a cleanup migration runs. Related open #12358 adds exactly such a migration; #12472 cleans it on reinstall, not on upgrade.

leads.summary: A missing aarch64 edge package or transient HEAD error permanently stamps the Sunshine migration complete
leads.consequence: Current edge/aarch64 advertises Sunshine 2026.516.143833-4.1, not the pinned 2026.914.233613-1 (whose URL is HTTP 404). For an existing arm user with vulnerable Sunshine, every failed HEAD, including 404, 403 and timeout, takes exit 0 on aarch64 without upgrading. omarchy-migrate writes the completion marker on exit 0; after the build is published this migration is not retried. Installation also proceeds to enable the still-old service and open ports. On x86_64 the current pinned package and its signature both return HTTP 200 and probe failure exits 1 for retry.
leads.triage: already in Opus final (F2 aarch64); corroboration

leads.summary: A failed local pacman query is treated as Sunshine absent and stamps the migration done
leads.consequence: `pacman -Q sunshine` can return nonzero for a query/database error, not only for a missing package. The migration silences both stdout and stderr and exits 0 in either case. omarchy-migrate writes the marker, skips the helper entirely, and will never reattempt the floor upgrade after the database fault clears. Direct calls to the helper also suppress `pacman -Qq` errors with `|| true`. Separate genuine absence from query failure so recoverable errors leave migration pending.
leads.triage: synthetic pacman db-error premise, low value; dropped

leads.summary: Combining the diverged open PR #12358 leaves its new Sunshine autostart test failing
leads.consequence: #12358's new test rejects any `systemctl --user disable --now sunshine` command, but this head deliberately retains that legacy alias disable immediately after canonical disable. Its test exits 1 before testing the cleanup migration against a head with this remover. Both PRs edit the same install and remove blocks, so resolution must coordinate the alias policy and tests (while preserving #12358's migration that clears old Hyprland starts). Compare API says diverged, not stacked; GitHub reports #12358 mergeable against its own base, not that the two PRs merge cleanly.
leads.triage: factual, verified by coordinator (pr-12358 test rejects `disable --now sunshine` which remove:64 keeps) and by Opus self-check source read; published

leads.summary: Installer fixture cannot exercise its failure-continuation contract and asserts an alias branch absent on installed hosts
leads.consequence: The security helper stub always exits 0, so the test passes even if an installer regression aborts on a failed floor upgrade; the failure path that motivated the follow-up is untested. A plausible mutant changing the install fallback to `exit 1` passed both install cases. Scenario two also requires `enable --now sunshine` (alias), but a real installed Sunshine package has the canonical unit under /usr/lib/systemd/user, so source install:67-68 always chooses canonical instead and that scenario fails on machines with Sunshine installed. Add explicit helper-failure case and control the unit-file check in the test.
leads.triage: helper-stub-always-succeeds verified from diff; published as source logic (Sol mutant run not relied on); fixed-path part already in Opus

leads.summary: Security upgrade test stays green when the helper never upgrades anything
leads.consequence: All checks inspect presence of literal strings in three source files, rather than run the helper with installed-old, provider, HEAD error, architecture or failed-pacman inputs. Injecting `exit 0` immediately after the helper's `set -euo pipefail` leaves every literal intact; the security test still exits 0 even though it never queries pacman or enforces the security floor. Add sandboxed mock pacman/curl/vercmp cases and marker status assertions.
leads.triage: already in Opus (F5); published as source logic

leads.summary: Migration's displayed security floor and edge-version description are stale
leads.consequence: The migration prints `2026.516 security floor` and comments that edge has 2026.906.222525, while the helper now uses 2026.914.233613-1 and the current x86_64 edge database lists the latter. This is misleading during an update and makes the recorded rationale contradict the actual version enforced; update the banner and comment to the new floor. The source date was 2026-09-27, and these repository versions can change later.

leads.summary: Another open Sunshine test has no stub for this new helper if both PRs merge
leads.consequence: #8879's test stubs systemctl, pkg-add/drop and webapp calls but not omarchy-pkg-upgrade-sunshine-security. If both diverged PRs are integrated with this test unchanged and a real helper is on PATH on an older Sunshine install, running the test can invoke real pacman, curl and sudo from the test. When the helper is absent it soft-continues with command-not-found instead, giving no coverage of upgrading. Set a helper stub and prevent network/package-manager access in the combined fixture.

limits: Full test/cli run under review.py exited 1 on missing theme directories before reaching its metadata loop (cli-run-log.txt), but focused commands --check and JSON metadata probes passed; this is not attributed to Sunshine.
#8879 test hazard is conditional on the actual merge resolution and PATH/install state, hence H7 is explicitly a hypothesis rather than an observed unsafe run.

flags.claim: So every existing install that has the line also has the unit enabled
flags.why: The absolute holds only for lines the old installer wrote, and only at the time it wrote them: the installer appended the line after `systemctl --user enable --now sunshine` succeeded under set -e (base d201fb9 bin/omarchy-install-service-sunshine lines 6, 74, 84). A user could have added the line by hand or disabled the unit later. My own handback stated the same absolute without this qualifier (internal inconsistency on my side).
flags.disposition: real error, fixed (qualified 'every install where the earlier installer wrote the line')

flags.why: `omarchy-refresh-hyprland` runs `omarchy-refresh-config hypr/autostart.lua`, which backs up and overwrites the whole file with the Omarchy default, so it also drops the line (along with any other customization). No update step or migration removes it, and the remove script is the only thing that strips just that line.
flags.disposition: real error, fixed (refresh-hyprland also resets file)

flags.claim: `omarchy-channel-set` and `omarchy-reinstall-pkgs` run `pacman -Syyuu` ... After that, Sunshine is back at `2026.516.143833-4.1` ... a channel switch silently reverts it.
flags.why: (a) Only switching to or re-selecting stable or rc (both list 2026.516.143833-4.1), or omarchy-reinstall-pkgs on those channels, reverts it; switching to edge keeps 2026.914.233613-1 because edge lists it. (b) Not silent: pacman prints 'warning: sunshine: downgrading from version ... to version ...' (pacman v7.1.0 lib/libalpm/sync.c:111); what is silent is that nothing re-applies the floor. (c) Minor attribution: both commands reach -Syyuu through omarchy-refresh-pacman (bin/omarchy-refresh-pacman:50; bin/omarchy-channel-set:133; bin/omarchy-reinstall-pkgs:11, which also runs -Suu at :14).
flags.disposition: real error, fixed (stable/rc only; pacman prints downgrade; later split into own heading and qualified as source conclusion)

flags.claim: only re-running the installer applies the floor again
flags.why: Among Omarchy commands this is right (the helper's only callers are bin/omarchy-install-service-sunshine:81 and migrations/1789400200.sh:12). But once stable or rc ship >= 2026.914.233613, a normal `omarchy update` (-Syu) restores it, and switching to edge does too. Minor.
flags.disposition: fixed ('Until stable or rc ship the fix')

flags.claim: Other migrations use `systemctl --user try-restart <unit>` for this.
flags.why: Plural is too strong for try-restart: only migrations/1789130779.sh:8 uses `systemctl --user try-restart` (wireplumber after a conf.d change). migrations/1784521870.sh:9 and 1785608166.sh:53 use `systemctl --user restart`. Minor.

flags.claim: Its `.sig` is from the Omarchy key
flags.why: I parsed the OpenPGP signature packet: its issuer fingerprint subpacket is 40DFB630FF42BCFFB047046CF0134EE680CAC571 (the Omarchy key per manual/48-security.md:31), the same issuer as the stable package's .sig. I did not cryptographically verify the signature; pacman does that at install. Nitpick; the earlier review used the same wording.
flags.disposition: fixed ('names the Omarchy key as issuer')

flags.claim: A small table test with stubbed `pacman`/`curl`/`sudo` could cover the provider skip, the x86_64 and aarch64 probe failures, and a failed `pacman -U`.
flags.why: Dropped part of the suggestion: the aarch64 branch is selected by `arch=$(uname -m)` (helper:32), so `uname` must be stubbed too (my fixture stubs pacman, curl, sudo and uname). Also 'only greps source strings' ignores the `-x`/`-f` checks at test lines 11 and 31; negligible.

flags.claim: Strip the exact line in the installer ..., and add a migration that strips it for existing installs.
flags.why: Lost qualifier from my report (optional): a safer migration strips the line only when the canonical unit is enabled, so a user who later disabled the unit and relies on the Hyprland line alone does not lose autostart; #12358's 1789703649.sh strips unconditionally. Supporting evidence not in the draft: the maintainer plan plans/remote.md:36 (commit f4f3d4c7, 2026-08-23) calls for a migration deleting this line from existing users' autostart.lua. flags.why: I only searched the Omarchy repository (docs/agents/manual); no statement about pkgs.omarchy.org retention exists there. I cannot say no policy is documented anywhere. Minor.
flags.disposition: fixed (Omarchy repository documents no retention policy)

flags.why: Verified for the Omarchy repository database only (pkgs.omarchy.org/{stable,rc}/aarch64/omarchy.db list no sunshine). The Arch-side aarch64 mirror was not checked (stable-mirror aarch64 extra.db returned 404). Nitpick.

## Automated AI review

> **Community review:** Independent automated community review, unaffiliated with the Omarchy team, intended to help prepare PRs for their review.

Follow-up to the [earlier review](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12271#issuecomment-5833236380) and the [author's reply](https://github.com/omacom/omarchy/pull/12271#issuecomment-5835116329), checked at head `d1edce3`.

**Outcome:** **Verified** on `d1edce3`: the new revision fixes the double start for new installs, the helper's failure handling and the stale pin. Four points remain: installs that already have both start paths are not repaired, the hard-coded pin can now block later migrations if the file disappears, switching to stable or rc reverts the upgrade, and the install test still depends on the host.

| Earlier finding | Status on `d1edce3` |
|---|---|
| 1. Two start paths at login | **Resolved** for new installs and reinstalls. Existing installs keep the old line (see below). |
| 2. Helper failure outcomes | **Resolved** on x86_64. aarch64 still records the migration as done when the probe fails. |
| 3. Pinned edge build unlisted | **Resolved for now.** The file name is still hard-coded (see below). |
| 4. Install test depends on the host | **Partly resolved.** The helper is mocked, but the fixed unit path remains. |
| Optional: grep-only security test | Unchanged. |
| Repository conventions (mode, `requires-sudo`) | **Resolved.** |

**Verified** (source, plus sandboxed runs of the real helper, install script and `omarchy-migrate` with stubbed `pacman`, `curl`, `sudo` and `uname`):
- The installer no longer writes `o.launch_on_start("sunshine")`, and the new test checks for its absence after both install runs.
- A failed x86_64 probe (404, DNS failure, timeout) now exits 1, as a failed `pacman -U` already did. `omarchy-migrate` writes no marker, stops the queue as `agents/skills/migrations.md` requires, and a later run in which the file is available completes normally.
- When the helper fails, the installer prints a warning and still enables the unit, opens the firewall ports and installs the web app.
- An AUR provider such as `sunshine-git` is skipped. `pacman -Qq sunshine` prints the provider's name (pacman 7.1 `query.c` falls back to `alpm_find_satisfier`), so the `!= sunshine` check works.
- The new floor `2026.914.233613-1` is the build the edge x86_64 database lists as of 2026-09-27. Its `.sig` names the Omarchy key as issuer, and its added dependencies are available on the stable mirror. Upstream advisory GHSA-fp6g-27w5-489j lists `v2026.914.233613` as the patched version.
- The migration is now mode 0644, and the helper declares `# omarchy:requires-sudo=true`.

**Author reply:** All four stated changes are confirmed. Two limits apply: "systemd-only start" covers new installs and reinstalls only, and "probe failures retry the migration" holds on x86_64 only. On aarch64 a failed probe is still a deliberate soft skip. The edge aarch64 database lists `2026.516.143833-4.1`, and the pinned aarch64 URL returns 404. The stable and rc Omarchy repositories list no aarch64 Sunshine package, so this mainly affects edge users.

### Existing installs keep the second start path

The earlier installer ran `systemctl --user enable --now sunshine` under `set -e` and only then appended the Hyprland line. So every install where the earlier installer wrote the line had the unit enabled at that point, which is the setup reported in #7218. This PR stops writing the line, but nothing removes it:

```text
existing install, after this PR
├─ systemd user unit (enabled earlier)        → starts Sunshine
└─ ~/.config/hypr/autostart.lua line (kept)   → starts a second Sunshine
   ├─ migration 1789400200: upgrades the package only
   └─ re-running the installer: line still present (sandboxed run)
```

The double start follows from #7218's reports and the earlier installer's source; it was not reproduced here. The line surviving a reinstall was observed in a sandboxed run.

**Impact:** Users who already hit #7218 keep the competing second process after updating. No update or migration removes it. Only the remove script strips that single line (a full `omarchy-refresh-hyprland` resets the whole file).

**Suggested change:** Strip the exact line in the installer (reuse the remove script's `sed`), and add a migration that strips it for existing installs, for example only when the canonical unit is enabled. Open PR #12358 contains such a migration (`1789703649.sh`, which strips the line unconditionally). Its new test also fails against this PR's remove script, because it rejects the retained `systemctl --user disable --now sunshine` line. The two PRs need a coordinated resolution.

### The pinned file name can now block the migration queue

The helper still builds the URL from the pinned version, and a failed probe on x86_64 now exits 1. If edge stops serving `sunshine-2026.914.233613-1-x86_64.pkg.tar.zst` before stable and rc carry a fixed build, this migration fails on every run for x86_64 users below the floor. `omarchy-migrate` then stops there. Inside `omarchy update`, the error aborts everything after `omarchy-migrate`: orphan cleanup, status, service restarts, AUR updates, hooks and the reboot prompt.

This has not happened yet: as of 2026-09-27, edge still serves the older `2026.906.222525-1.1` and `2026.516.143833-4.1` files. But a failure that was a silent skip in the earlier revision is now a blocking one.

**Impact:** The fix depends on one edge file staying available. If it disappears first, every `omarchy update` on affected x86_64 installs stops at this migration.

**Suggested change:** Publishing `2026.914.233613` or newer to stable and rc removes the dependency without client code. If the client-side helper stays, read the current file name from the edge `omarchy.db` entry and require it to be at or above the floor, instead of building the URL from a fixed name.

### Switching to stable or rc reverts the upgrade

`omarchy-channel-set` and `omarchy-reinstall-pkgs` go through `omarchy-refresh-pacman`, which runs `pacman -Syyuu`. In pacman 7.1 source, `-uu` downgrades a package whose local version is newer than the repository's. On stable or rc, Sunshine would then return to `2026.516.143833-4.1` while the migration marker stays in place. This is a conclusion from pacman source, not an observed transaction.

**Impact:** Switching to or re-selecting stable or rc undoes the security upgrade, and nothing re-applies it. Until stable or rc ship the fix, only re-running the installer applies the floor again.

**Suggested change:** The same stable and rc publication fixes this.

**Optional:** The migration upgrades the package but does not restart the running user unit, so the old binary keeps running until the next login. Other migrations restart a running user service after a change (for example `1789130779.sh` uses `systemctl --user try-restart wireplumber.service`).

**Optional test improvement:** Two changes would make the tests catch real regressions:
- `sunshine-install-test.sh` still depends on the fixed host path `/usr/lib/systemd/user/app-dev.lizardbyte.app.Sunshine.service`. In a sandboxed copy with that path made injectable and the unit present, scenario 2 fails with `not ok - already-enabled sunshine.service is reused via its alias`. The helper mock always succeeds, so the test would still pass if the installer went back to aborting when the helper fails. Make the unit path injectable and add a failing-helper case.
- `sunshine-security-upgrade-test.sh` only greps source strings. A helper that exits 0 before checking anything would still pass, because the checked strings stay in the file. A small table test with stubbed `pacman`/`curl`/`sudo`/`uname` could cover the provider skip, the x86_64 and aarch64 probe failures, and a failed `pacman -U`.

**Stale text:** `migrations/1789400200.sh` still prints "past the 2026.516 security floor" and says edge has `2026.906.222525`. The floor is now `2026.914.233613`.

---

## Review information

**Test scope:** Follow-up source review of head `d1edce3` (base `d201fb9`), compared with the earlier reviewed PR diff on `08f91b7`. Pacman 7.1 source was read for query, sync and downgrade behavior. Omarchy stable, rc and edge package databases, the pinned package and its signature, and the stable mirror databases were fetched as data on 2026-09-27. Sandboxed runs without network covered the helper, the migration under `omarchy-migrate`, the install script and both PR tests, using synthetic `pacman`, `curl`, `sudo` and `uname` stubs. No real login session, systemd instance, pacman transaction or aarch64 system was used. The double start on existing installs is based on #7218's reports and the earlier installer's source, not on a reproduction. The `-Syyuu` downgrade is a conclusion from pacman source. Edge retention was checked once, and the Omarchy repository documents no retention policy.

**AI process:** Opus 5.5 Medium coordination and synthesis, Opus 5.5 Xhigh technical review and final fact check, GPT 6 Sol Xhigh search for related issues, Opus 5.5 Medium editorial check.

**Opt out:** To stop receiving these reviews, reply to this comment saying so.
